comment: Baseline count of `tsc --noEmit` (checkJs) errors. The typecheck enforcement test (tests/typecheck.test.js) asserts the current error count is <= this number. This is a RATCHET: it may only ever be lowered, never raised. New code must not introduce typecheck errors above the baseline; reducing the baseline by adding JSDoc annotations is encouraged. NEVER raise this number to make a failing build pass — fix the code or annotate instead.
notes: ZERO. Ratchet lowered 64 → 0 on 2026-07-14 (R2-Z, plan 00011-r2z-boundary-typecheck-zero). The R2 wave had pushed the live `tsc --noEmit` (checkJs) count to 94; all 94 were fixed at the SOURCE — JSDoc @param/@returns/@type/@typedef annotations, precise typedefs (approval-ledger's LedgerEntryInput, inbox's string-map frontmatter reader), literal-union narrowing, and a small number of documented one-line casts where the shape is genuinely dynamic (a field repurposed from accumulation Set to numeric cardinality, the heterogeneous area-module render hooks, Date−Date valueOf() arithmetic, raw command-line text, and an unvalidated string being membership-tested by the very call that validates it). No `@ts-ignore` and no `@ts-nocheck` appear anywhere in the tree — they hide errors instead of fixing them and are forbidden. Two documentation defects were corrected in passing: human-gate-check's checkFolder @returns omitted the `reason` field it actually returns (so the violation printout's reason was invisible to the type system), and dependency-auditor's mapPipSeverity was documented `@param {string}` while comparing its argument numerically against the 9/7/4 CVSS bands. The gate is now absolute: with the baseline at zero, ANY new type error fails `npm run typecheck`. It can never be raised — warnings are bugs, and time is a vector.
